You are the cold reviewer in the po-output-check process, step screen, round 1 (fresh context). Read only the three files named here — nothing else.

- criteria_path: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/fitness/backlog-order.fitness.md
- framing: /home/vscode/rebaseline/roadmap.md (the PM role's recorded priority)
- artifact: /home/vscode/rebaseline/backlog/order-2026-09-05.md

Step prompt (verbatim): "State, as judge_stamp, the model and prompt version you judge as. Read the criteria set at criteria_path, the framing at framing, and the artifact at artifact — nothing else. Judge the artifact against every criterion and against the framing: does each part of it trace to the framing, and does anything in it serve no framed outcome? Report every finding with the criterion it fails by name — "framing" for a part that does not trace to the framing or serves no framed outcome — the quoted text, the change, and whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the PM role decides from the review alone. A defect no criterion names is a finding with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean" only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top three changes."

Return exactly this structure:
judge_stamp: <model id> / screen prompt v6
verdict: clean | findings
findings:
- criterion: <scenario name or number, "framing", or "uncovered">
  section: <section of the artifact>
  quoted: "<the text>"
  change: <what would repair it>
  decided: confident | wobbly
top_three: <the three most important changes, or "none">

Be literal to the criteria. Do not invent criteria. Do not read any other file.

# Backlog order — 2026-09-05

This order supersedes [order-2026-09-04](order-2026-09-04.md), placed
against the priority's v3 of 2026-09-04; that order's one item —
init-request-routing's features-to-be — has since been taken up (its
feature authored, checked, and assigned; the initiative's measure met
2026-09-04 and its status now active), and the authority's bet of 2026-09-05 adds
a planned initiative to place.

## 1. Priority followed

The order is placed against the PM role's recorded roadmap priority,
v5 of 2026-09-05 ([roadmap.md](../roadmap.md)), which states:

1. **init-typedef-rendering** — the planned initiative; the authority's
   bet of 2026-09-05; the maker and the checker of an artifact work
   from the same standard, proven on the product decision record, on
   the authority's direction "The typedef rendering should go first."
2. **init-request-routing** — active; its measure met 2026-09-04; it
   stays in the priority until the PO role judges its feature done and
   the `completed` state lands.
3. **init-roles-availability** — active; its measure met 2026-09-03;
   as above.
4. **init-skills-availability** — active; its one feature assigned; as
   above.
5. **More comprehensive rendering work** — the authority's direction
   (bead lead-sx9xj); not yet framed as an initiative.

The priority also notes six requests routed and awaiting the
authority's answer, not yet in the priority, and records **ADR
artifact and processes** (bead lead-mfcyp) as delivered and removed —
so neither has a place here.

The order follows this priority with no exceptions. The priority's
item 2 has no untaken features-to-be: its one feature,
[feat-request-routing](../features/feat-request-routing.md), is
assigned (the feature's own status, v8; the initiative's Features line
still reads "checked") — taken up — its measure is met in the running
system (2026-09-04), and the initiative's Features section names no
other;
what remains for it is this role's judgment that its feature is done
and the pending `completed` state, neither of which is an item to
order. Item 3 likewise has no untaken features-to-be: its one feature,
[feat-roles-availability](../features/feat-roles-availability.md), is
assigned, its measure met (6 of 6, 2026-09-03), and the initiative's
Features section names no other. Item 4 likewise: its one feature,
[feat-skills-availability](../features/feat-skills-availability.md),
is assigned, and the initiative's Features section names no other. A
further feature authored under any of the three would enter a
superseding order in that initiative's priority position. Item 5 is
not an order item: it has no framed initiative and no planned status,
so there are no features-to-be to place — it stands in the priority as
a thing yet to frame and enters a future order once an initiative for
it is planned. The six routed requests are likewise not order items:
none has an initiative, and a request is the PM role's to answer
before anything reaches this role for ordering. All of these are
consequences of what exists to place, not inversions of the priority.

## 2. Enabler recommendations received

Record absent: none received. No enabler-recommendations record
exists from the solutions architect role, and none have been
communicated through its interface with this role. There is therefore
nothing to place or decline. The initiative's Feasibility section
names the three documents that fold into the typedef and the compiler
the build follows; those are the architect's feasibility evidence
attached to the framing, not enabler recommendations to this role, and
they enter this order only as the work item 1's features-to-be will
specify. Should the architect raise an omitted recommendation against
this order (the typedef's raising rule), the order will be superseded
with the recommendation placed or declined with reasons.

## 3. The order

**Item 1 — init-typedef-rendering: features-to-be.**

- **Framing served:** the planned initiative
  [init-typedef-rendering](../initiatives/init-typedef-rendering.md)
  (status: planned, v9; the authority's bet of 2026-09-05 — "Bet" —
  recorded in that initiative's history at v9; no product decision
  record links yet, because by the initiative's Appetite that record
  is the proof itself, made and screened from the one standard once
  the rendering exists). Its framing: whoever makes an artifact and
  whoever checks it work from different words, because the standard
  for an artifact type is written in several places by hand, and a
  change to it does not reliably reach both; the outcome is the maker
  and the checker of an artifact working from the same standard, a
  change to the standard reaching both, and the checker's tests — the
  fitness set's scenarios — runnable by the author first; proven on
  the product decision record, target 1 of 22 types.
- **Owning context:** none — lead-shop-internal. The ruling this
  entry follows is the initiative's Decomposition section: the
  solutions architect role's attached ruling, screened and bet on by
  the authority, which states no Bounded Context is touched — the
  typedef, the compiler, and the renderings sit in the lead shop's
  tree, and no contract exists on this branch to rely on; cross-context
  flow none. An item the architect's decomposition places in no
  Bounded Context has nothing to assign across and nothing to
  escalate. Not a cross-context item; no escalation applies.
- **Readiness (first untaken item):** **not ready.** No feature exists
  yet — the initiative's Features section reads "None yet." It waits
  on feature authoring of the initiative's first feature in the
  feature-authoring process and that feature's pass through the PO
  output check.

No other items. Nothing was declined: the only planned initiative is
placed, each active initiative's one feature is already taken up, and
no other requirement has reached this role for ordering.
